Enishi International School · Staff guide

How to update the EIS Compass calendar

A step-by-step guide for staff. You do not need any technical knowledge. It takes about 10 minutes the first time and 3–5 minutes after that.

In this guide

  • What is EIS Compass?The 3 files and what they do
  • 5 important rulesRead these first
  • Part A · Edit the spreadsheetAdd or change events
  • Part B · Update the websiteUse the admin page
  • Part C · A quick fixChange one event without Excel
  • Problems and questionsAnswers to common questions

What is EIS Compass?

EIS Compass is the school's online events calendar. Families open it on their phone or computer at enishi.ac.jp/EISCompass.html. It is in English and Japanese.

To update it, you use three files:

1. The spreadsheetEIS-Compass-events.xlsxAn Excel file with one row per event. This is where you write events.
2. The admin pageadmin.htmlA tool that opens in your web browser. It turns your spreadsheet into the website page.
3. The website pageEISCompass.htmlThe calendar families see. The admin page makes a new copy of this file every time you update.

The whole process is:

Edit the spreadsheet → open the admin page → import → check → download → upload to the website

There is no login or password.The admin page works on your own computer. It cannot change the website by itself, so you cannot break the live calendar by trying things. Nothing changes for families until the new file is uploaded.

5 important rules

  1. Always start from the newest files. Use the newest spreadsheet and the newest EISCompass.html from the shared EIS Compass folder. If you use an old copy, you will undo other people's changes.
  2. One person at a time. Tell your team before you start an update, so two people do not update at the same time.
  3. Never change the id column. It keeps links working. For a new event, leave id empty — the admin page fills it in.
  4. Write English and Japanese. Families read both. If you do not write Japanese, ask a Japanese-speaking colleague. The admin page will remind you if Japanese is missing.
  5. Save the new files back to the shared folder. After you update, put the new spreadsheet and the new EISCompass.html back in the shared folder, so the next person starts from them.

AEdit the spreadsheet

Open EIS-Compass-events.xlsx in Excel (or Google Sheets). It has three tabs at the bottom:

  • Events — one row for each event. You will use this most.
  • Holidays — days with no school (national holidays, school holidays, staff days).
  • Guide — a short reminder of what to write in each column.

What to write in each column (Events tab)

ColumnWhat to writeExample
idDo not touch. Leave empty for a new event.2026-10-21-college-fair
startThe date of the event (year-month-day).2026-10-21
endThe last day. For a one-day event, write the same date as start.2026-10-21
timeOptional. A start time, or start and end. Empty = all day.15:00  or  15:00-17:00
audiencesWho the event is for. Separate with commas. Use these words: Whole School, ELC, Primary, Secondary, High School, PTA, Community Club.Primary, ELC
parents_invitedWrite yes if parents can come. Otherwise leave empty.yes
no_classesWrite yes if students have no classes that day.yes
statusUsually empty. Or: tentative (not confirmed yet), cancelled.cancelled
title_en / title_jaThe event name in English and Japanese.College Fair / 大学進学フェア
description_en / description_jaOne or two sentences about the event, in English and Japanese.Universities visit our school…
location_en / location_jaOptional. Where it happens.Gym / 体育館
imageOptional. Ask the website manager to add photos.
link_1, link_2, link_3Optional. A link to a flyer, sign-up form or more information. It shows as a button when families open the event.https://forms.gle/…
hiddenWrite yes to keep an event as a draft (families do not see it).yes

Common tasks

Add a new event — Add a new row at the bottom. Leave id empty. Fill in the dates, audiences, and the titles and descriptions in both languages. The order of the rows does not matter.
Change a date — Change start and end. When you import, the admin page can show families a “Date changed” label with the old date.
Cancel an event — Write cancelled in status. Families will see “Cancelled” and the title crossed out. (This is better than deleting the row, because families who saw the event will understand what happened.)
Remove an event completely — Delete the whole row. The admin page will show it as “removed” before anything changes.
An event over several days — Put the first day in start and the last day in end, e.g. 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13.
Add a time — Type it in time, e.g. 15:00 or 15:00-17:00. Use the 24-hour clock.
Add a flyer or sign-up form — Paste the web address into link_1. To choose the button text, write Flyer | チラシ | https://… (English text | Japanese text | address). If the flyer is on Google Drive, set sharing to “Anyone with the link”.
CarefulDo not rename or move the column headings in the first row. The admin page finds each column by its heading.

When you are finished, save the spreadsheet (Ctrl+S on Windows, ⌘+S on Mac).

BUpdate the website

Now you use the admin page to turn your spreadsheet into the new website page.

1

Open the admin page

Double-click admin.html. It opens in your web browser (Chrome, Edge or Safari). You do not need the internet for this.

2

Open the current calendar

On the 1 · Open tab, drag the newest EISCompass.html into the dashed box, or click Choose file… and select it.

Why this step?The website page carries all the events inside it. The admin page reads it so it knows what is on the website now.
3

Import your spreadsheet

The 2 · Events tab shows every event. Click Import spreadsheet… and choose your saved EIS-Compass-events.xlsx.

4

Look at the changes, then apply

A window shows what will change: new events, changed events (old value in red, new value in green) and removed events. Read it carefully.

  • If it looks right, click Apply import.
  • If something is wrong, click Cancel, fix the spreadsheet, save it, and import again.
“Date changed” labelLeave the tick box on. Then families see “Date changed (was …)” next to any event whose date moved.
5

Check for problems

Open the 3 · Check tab. It lists anything that looks wrong:

  • Errors (red) — must be fixed. For example a wrong date, or an event with no audience. You cannot publish until they are fixed.
  • Warnings (orange) — please look. For example a missing Japanese title, or two events with the same description.
  • Notes (grey) — just information. Usually fine.

Click an event name to open and fix it. You can also fix it in the spreadsheet and import again.

6

Download the new files

Open the 4 · Publish tab. Check the “Last updated” date (it is today's date), then click Download everything (.zip).

A zip file downloads to your Downloads folder, named like EIS-Compass-publish-2026-10-07.zip. It contains the new EISCompass.html and the calendar files that families subscribe to.

7

Put the files on the website

Send the zip file to the website manager, who will upload it. (If you have been given website access, upload the files yourself, keeping the same folders.)

Then:

  • Save the new EISCompass.html and your spreadsheet in the shared EIS Compass folder, replacing the old ones (see Rule 5).
  • After the upload, open the calendar on your phone and check one event you changed.
  • For important changes (for example a cancelled event), also tell families on Toddle as usual.
Done!Families who subscribed to the calendar on their phone will get the changes automatically. Google Calendar can take up to a day to show them.

CA quick fix without the spreadsheet

For a small change to one event (for example a spelling mistake or a new time), you can edit it directly in the admin page:

  1. Do steps 1 and 2 of Part B (open the admin page and the current calendar).
  2. On the 2 · Events tab, click the event. Use the search box or the month menu to find it.
  3. Change what you need and click Save. To add a new event, click + Add event.
  4. Do steps 5–7 of Part B (check, download, upload).
  5. Important: click Download as Excel on the Events tab and save it as the new spreadsheet in the shared folder. If you skip this, the next person's spreadsheet will not have your fix, and their import will undo it.

Problems and questions

I closed the browser in the middle. Did I lose my work?

No. The admin page remembers your unfinished work in that browser on that computer. Open admin.html again and continue. (To start fresh, go to the 1 · Open tab and click Discard local changes.)

The import says “unknown audience”.

Check the spelling in the audiences column. Use only: Whole School, ELC, Primary, Secondary, High School, PTA, Community Club. Separate them with commas.

The import says a date was “not understood”.

Write dates as year-month-day, for example 2026-11-03. Also check that start is not empty.

The import shows many “removed” events that I did not delete.

You probably opened an old or wrong spreadsheet, or the wrong tab. Click Cancel — nothing has changed yet. Get the newest spreadsheet from the shared folder and try again.

I uploaded, but the website still shows the old calendar.

Your browser may be showing a saved copy. Reload the page (on a phone, pull down to refresh; on a computer press Ctrl+F5 or ⌘+Shift+R). If it is still old, ask the website manager to check the upload.

I made a mistake and it is already on the website.

Don't worry. Fix it in the spreadsheet or the admin page and publish again — the new upload replaces the old one. If it is urgent, ask the website manager to put back the previous version.

I don't write Japanese.

Fill in the English and ask a Japanese-speaking colleague to add the Japanese titles and descriptions. The Check tab shows which events are missing Japanese.

Can I use Google Sheets instead of Excel?

Yes. Upload the spreadsheet to Google Drive, open it with Google Sheets, and when you are finished choose File → Download → Microsoft Excel (.xlsx). Import that file.

A photo looks small or does not show in the event window.

Photos are optional. Only good-quality photos (wide enough) appear large in the event window. Ask the website manager if you want to add or change a photo.

Should I upload admin.html to the website?

No. The admin page stays on your computer or in the shared folder. Only the files in the zip go on the website.

Who to ask

Website manager: Beksultan Shaimardan — for uploading files, photos, website access, and anything in this guide that is unclear.

Keep this guide in the shared EIS Compass folder next to admin.html.
